analysis: The PR changes only documentation: docs/provider/troubleshooting.md (head lines 3, 170-172) and docs/reference/configuration.md (patch hunks at lines 1-6 and 198-201). No executable code, keys, attestation paths or wire protocol is touched. The diff updates the 'Last updated' dates, adds two troubleshooting rows (head lines 171-172) for provider 0.10.6 and earlier following coordinator model rollouts, and expands the `backend.enabled_models` row in configuration.md. The new text says a nonempty `enabled_models` acts as an operator filter: without Autopilot, coordinator `load_model`, `prefetch_model` and `desired_models` never load, download or advertise a model outside it. The docs cite ProviderLoop+ModelSelection.swift `operatorFilterAllows`, which was not supplied, so I could not verify the implementation matches the described behavior. Threat-model relevance: TB-002 coordinator-to-provider commands and A-004 model weights / T-027 model substitution. A trusted coordinator pushing models outside the operator filter is the older, documented behavior (0.10.6 and earlier). The docs describe a mitigation, but the code change is outside this batch. The documentation does not weaken a control and adds no new attack surface. Remaining question for integration: whether the code change, not in this batch, enforces the filter on all coordinator-driven load, download and advertise paths, including desired_models alias successors. This is not a finding here. The T-041 mention of SSD cache defaults is unchanged and consistent with the existing troubleshooting text.
